pool.text: French traders built the first fort, Fort Rouge, on the site.
A settlement was founded by the Selkirk settlers of the Red River Colony.
On November 8, Winnipeg was incorporated as a city with the Selkirk settlement.
The Winnipeg Art Gallery was founded as Western Canada's oldest public art gallery.
The Pantages Playhouse Theatre opened as a vaudeville house in the city.
Canada's first jazz concert took place at the Pantages Playhouse Theatre.
More than 30,000 workers walked off their jobs in the Winnipeg general strike.
The Manitoba Legislative Building opened, constructed mainly of Tyndall stone.
Le Cercle Molière was founded in St Boniface as Canada's oldest theatre company.
The Victory Loan Campaign staged a mock Nazi invasion of Winnipeg to promote awareness.
Television broadcasting in Winnipeg started with CBWT going on the air.
Winnipeg became the first Canadian host of the Pan American Games.
The Royal Canadian Mint was established, producing all circulating coinage in Canada.
The reclamation and redevelopment of CNR rail yards turned the Forks into a tourist attraction.
The 30-block Exchange District received National Historic Site of Canada status.
The City of Winnipeg Act was repealed and replaced with the City of Winnipeg Charter.
Winnipeg was named the Cultural Capital of Canada by Canadian Heritage.
KPMG ranked Winnipeg as the least expensive location to do business in western Canada.
The Canadian Museum for Human Rights opened to the public in September.
The city started to deal with an increasingly large methamphetamine problem fueling violent crime.
